title: Bob Rolontz's label and Champion Jack Dupree's "Lonely Road Blues"
summary: McRae recalls producing for Rolontz, taking Dupree to record "Lonely Road Blues" and Dupree's "When I Get Married".

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: trouble was, when we did this date with Mickey Baker and all those people -- the first time I did this date, everybody wanted to know who was the star. Because I had been doing recording dates. You know, I was writing for -- See, I was writing for a lot of dates, you know. And so when I went down to do -- When Bob Rolontz got this label, I took Jack Dupree over there. We made one -- I made one side, 'The Same Old Road' (inaudible). Didn't I bring you a record on that? The one side we did? I think I did. I think I gave you a record --
Yeah. I gave you a 45 on that --
Jack Dupree and Mr. Bear, 'Lonely Road Blues'.
Yeah. 'When I Get Married,' that's Jack's side by himself. I did a side with Jack,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

'Lonely Road Blues,' (inaudible) talked and talked to him -- on that road again -- something like that. On the other side, he did by himself, 'When I Got Married.' That's by Jack Dupree. The number is 4G0171. 4G-0171.
And Bob Rolontz is spelled -- his name is spelled how?
Okay. Not a very common name. So, a number of these things were recorded also with Jack Dupree.
'55. Was he known as Champion Jack Dupree at that time?
